target.name: ByteCodeInterpreter flag-mask application (sub_08003310)
target.role: apply a mask to a run of flag bits: set where a bit is 1, clear where it is 0
target.notes: sub_08003310, 86 bytes and 41 instructions, one terminator at 0x08003364, native dispatch entry 187, calls the already-lifted setter sub_08004380 and clearer sub_08004396, one literal 0x08054FBC. It begins IMMEDIATELY WHERE THE GATHER ENDS at 0x08003310, and it is the first consumer of the mask that gather pushes. STACK BEHAVIOUR: it POPPED three values in order - the MASK from the stack top, then the WIDTH, then the BIT OFFSET - and pushes NOTHING, so the counter moves by exactly -3 and the mask is never written back to the stack. MASK INTERPRETATION: it is not merely tested or stored. The routine applies it per bit: for i = 0..width-1 it SETS the flag at (offset + i) when mask bit i is 1 and CLEARS it when that bit is 0, so EACH BIT OF THE MASK BECOMES THE STATE OF THE CORRESPONDING FLAG. That makes it the exact counterpart of the gather that produced it, and it is the first concrete engine consequence of the gathered mask. The bit under test is always mask bit 0, because `lsls r2, r4, #0x1f` moves it into bit 31 for the `beq` and `asrs r4, r4, #1` then brings the next bit down. TWO CLAMPS, BOTH SIGNED: a mask that is negative when read as signed is replaced by 0 entirely, and a mask where (1 << width) is not greater is truncated to (1 << width) - 1. ORDERING: all three pops complete before the first flag is touched, and the offset is added to the loop index immediately before each call. WIDTH 32 IS A REAL EDGE CASE, reproduced rather than corrected: ARM LSL by a register yields ZERO for an amount of 32 or more, so at a width of 32 the width clamp computes 0 - 1 = 0xFFFFFFFF EVEN FOR A MASK OF 0, and `asrs` keeps it all ones, so all 32 flags are SET. A width of zero or less is skipped entirely by the `ble`, though the three values are still consumed. THE THUMB SHIFT IS MODELLED EXPLICITLY rather than left to C, because `1u << 32` is undefined in C and MSVC masks the amount to five bits and yields 1, which is the opposite of the machine. NO BOUNDS CHECK and no NULL check. UNKNOWN: what the flags mean, and how large the array is. No semantic name is assigned, and nothing is imported from another title.
